parsed.why: Seat-of-government division: no local bathroom ban, but a national-legislature-imposed facilities restriction that local law cannot repeal, with a 2024 arrest and national overrides. Documented national passport and entry exposure applies. Stands under parent regime; local protections count only as uncertain mitigation.

Strong documented protections in force: gender-identity nondiscrimination in public accommodations, hate-crime coverage, panic-defence repeal, self-determination marker change, shield laws, and no facility restriction. Parent passport and entry exposure still applies, so it sits below the top band.

Parent regime applies; state has no bathroom ban for adults, with broad gender-identity protections and accessible markers. Offsets are restricted by youth-targeting school and athletics rules and a 2026 policy reversal pending. Youth-only restrictions are mid-level exposure.

Universal-exposure facility ban reaching public buildings with complaint-based enforcement and a public reporting form inviting reports on trans people. Documentary defence unavailable to visitors. Forced care denial for minors, retroactive suits, and state-level hostile laws and an arrest-like pattern push it into High Risk.

Facility ban expanded in 2026 to universities and sits on a prior restriction; prison freeze-frame treatment restrictions and no hate-crime statute. Documented escalation outweighs the local protections in some municipalities. Parent regime applies; no state-level sodomy enforcement but unrepealed statute is secondary.
